title: Thin structure
opening: When the camera and tripod are ready, a thought and one real example can carry you straight into recording. The example gives the thought something concrete to show, and watching the video lets you see whether the explanation reaches its ending. A small structure earns its place when it gets the work finished at the quality it needs.

labels.comparisonIntro: The task is to explain one thought with a real example. Compare a bare start, a complete thin structure and a larger arrangement for repeated class delivery.
labels.practice: Design a structure for today’s work
labels.practiceIntro: Name the trigger, the direction that carries the work, and a clear ending. Keep every quality and rights requirement. Add a step only when its function is needed.
labels.private: This private note is optional. The six required course questions are separate.
labels.length: This full note is over 2,000 characters. Shorten it to save; all of your text stays here.
labels.sourceQuote:
What looks spontaneous can still have an input, a process and an output. You may only need a thin structure: a small trigger that gets you started, enough direction to work through the middle, and a clear way to end. Leave room to respond to what happens.
Try it with a thought you already want to explain:
1. Have the camera and tripod ready. Keep the lessons from earlier attempts and the quality the work requires.
2. Choose the thought and one real example. You can show the work you are already doing; you do not have to invent a separate activity to record.
3. Decide what starts the recording, what you will explain and where you will end. Press record when the thought comes. State it, show the example and finish the explanation.
4. Watch what you made. Did the example make the thought clear? Did you reach the ending? Use the result to improve the next attempt.
Reduce the delay between thought and action while still doing the work fully. A thin structure must get you to a finished result with the required quality. A larger method needs the same check: what has it actually produced?

labels.bareTrigger: Press record as soon as the thought appears.
labels.bareDirection: Speak without choosing an example or deciding what the explanation needs to cover.
labels.bareEnding: Stop when the recording feels finished; do not inspect it.
labels.bareQuality: No example check, source check or permission check has been done.
labels.bareEarned: The file may exist quickly, but the missing example and checks leave the required quality unproven. This is incomplete, not thin.
labels.thinTrigger: The camera is ready; start when the thought and one real example are ready.
labels.thinDirection: State the thought, show the real example, and explain the relationship. Keep lessons from earlier attempts.
labels.thinEnding: Watch the recording. Check that the example makes the thought clear and that the explanation reaches its ending; revise if it does not.
labels.thinQuality: Keep the required source and permission checks, along with the quality needed for this explanation.
labels.thinEarned: Each step starts, carries, or checks the work. The setup stays small because a ready camera and an existing example supply what the task needs.
labels.expandedTrigger: A shared lesson is ready for several class groups on a set schedule.
labels.expandedDirection: Plan a delivery time for each class and prepare captions so learners can access the explanation. Give each group a way to send a question.
labels.expandedEnding: Check that the example makes the thought clear, the captions carry it, and every class knows where to send questions.
labels.expandedQuality: Keep the quality and permission requirements that apply to the work, and make the explanation accessible to each class.
labels.expandedEarned: Captions support learners who need them; a schedule and question route support repeated class sessions. If the work has neither need, those steps add delay.
labels.observation: A larger structure still earns its place by what it produces. A smaller one needs added support when it repeatedly misses an important requirement.

example.task: I want to explain one idea using an example from work already in progress. The thought and example are ready; the camera and tripod are available.
example.direction: State the idea, show the real example and explain how it supports the point. Retain the useful lesson from the previous unclear recording.
example.ending: Watch the recording. If the example makes the idea clear and the explanation reaches its end, it is ready; otherwise revise the relevant part.
example.requirements: Check the source and permission for any material shown, and keep the audio and example clear enough for the intended viewer.
example.extra: A large production system is unnecessary for one explanation. A shared course for many groups may warrant caption review, source records and a response route because those steps support access and repeated delivery.

modes.label: Fast start, incomplete work
modes.trigger: Press record as soon as the thought appears.
modes.direction: Speak without choosing an example or deciding what the explanation needs to cover.
modes.ending: Stop when the recording feels finished; do not inspect it.
modes.quality: Keep any source, permission or quality requirements the work needs; these have not been checked.
modes.result: A video file exists, but whether it explains the thought clearly is unknown.
modes.earned: The file may exist quickly, but the missing example and checks leave the required quality unproven. This is incomplete, not thin.

modes.label: Thin and complete
modes.trigger: The camera is ready; start when the thought and one real example are ready.
modes.direction: State the thought, show the real example, and explain the relationship. Keep lessons from earlier attempts.
modes.ending: Watch the recording. Check that the example makes the thought clear and that the explanation reaches its ending; revise if it does not.
modes.quality: Keep the required source and permission checks, along with the quality needed for this explanation.
modes.result: A clear explanation that reaches its ending, or a specific part to improve before sharing.
modes.earned: Each step starts, carries, or checks the work. The setup stays small because a ready camera and an existing example supply what the task needs.

modes.label: Larger, warranted structure
modes.trigger: A shared lesson is ready for several class groups on a set schedule.
modes.direction: Plan a delivery time for each class and prepare captions so learners can access the explanation. Give each group a way to send a question.
modes.ending: Check that the example makes the thought clear, the captions carry it, and every class knows where to send questions.
modes.quality: Keep the quality and permission requirements that apply to the work, and make the explanation accessible to each class.
modes.result: One explanation prepared for the scheduled classes, with captions and a clear route for questions. Check whether it serves each class.
modes.earned: Captions support learners who need them; a schedule and question route support repeated class sessions. If the work has neither need, those steps add delay.
